title: 9% of UK Workers Got No Job Onboarding — Survey
paragraphs: It doesn't matter how qualified or experienced you are — everyone needs some guidance when they start a new job.
However, a survey of 1,000 UK workers by human resources software company HBHR found that almost one in 10 got little or no onboarding for their job.

Onboarding is an important process in which new employees get the skills and knowledge they need to integrate into their new workplace and succeed in their jobs. This goes beyond a quick office tour on their first day, and is usually done over time, perhaps even across the employee's first year.

HBHR also found that it took the average employee a little over seven months to feel fully settled and productive in their current or most recent job — and almost one in 10 said it took them over a year. Also, 7% said they have never felt fully settled in.

The first few months in a new job can be difficult, as the survey also found that one in 10 UK workers had seriously considered leaving a role within their first month — and 9% actually left a job within their first three months.

A number of young workers pointed to onboarding issues as the problem. Fourteen percent of workers aged 18 to 24 said onboarding experiences had made them view an employer negatively, as did 16% of 25-to-35-year-olds.
Speaking to People Management, Simone Robinson from training company First Ascent Group said human resources staff should use a new employee's first month to help them navigate the organization.

"What seems obvious to a long-term employee can be essential guidance for newcomers. Start with the fundamentals of how things are done and feature the everyday practices of the most effective employees," she said.

HBHR's Callum Pennington also commented, "Training shouldn't be something employees complete when they join and then forget about. It should be part of how an organisation continuously develops its people."
